claims.text: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for united action on border security following mass migrant crossings into Ceuta.
Spain estimates that approximately 69,500 migrants have returned to Morocco after entering Ceuta.
The official death toll from the Ceuta border crisis stands at 72 on the Spanish side and 11 on the Moroccan side.
Italy temporarily suspended the Schengen border-free arrangement with Spain following the Ceuta migrant crossings.
Ceuta and Melilla represent the European Union's only land borders with Africa.
Spanish officials began installing a 500-metre floating barrier at the border with Morocco following the crossings.
Italy and Denmark organised a letter signed by 22 EU member states criticizing Spain's regularisation of undocumented migrants.
Ceuta's top government official Juan Jesus Vivas estimated that between 3,000 and 5,000 migrants remained in the city after initial returns.
The Moroccan Association for Human Rights reported nearly 130 victims and dozens missing from the Ceuta border rush.
Donald Trump stated that negotiations with Iran are ongoing and called them a last chance before decapitation.
Iran foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei denied direct talks with Washington and stated negotiations are with Oman over Strait of Hormuz passage.
The war between the United States and Iran began on February 28, 2026, following surprise strikes by the US and Israel.
Donald Trump called the Iranian leadership unbelievably duplicitous on Truth Social for denying negotiations.
Donald Trump stated he called off planned military strikes on Iran at the request of Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar.
Brent Crude oil fell by 4.5% to $83.98 per barrel following announcements regarding potential US-Iran negotiations.
Vessel crossings in the Strait of Hormuz dropped to 51 between July 30 and August 2 according to data from Kpler.
Seven people, including three children, were killed when drone debris struck a beach in Arkhipo-Osipovka.
A bombing at an Italian restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow killed five people and injured 19 others.
Reports indicated the Moscow restaurant bombing may have targeted Col Gen Alexander Chaiko during his 55th birthday celebration.
A drone struck a crowded beach near the Russian Black Sea resort of Gelendzhik.
Krasnodar region Governor Veniamin Kondratyev stated that 40 people were injured and 17 hospitalised in the Arkhipo-Osipovka beach strike.
A Ukrainian drone strike targeted a Wildberries warehouse in the Vladimir region overnight.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused NATO and the EU of participating in international terrorist activity following the beach strike.
Two crew members died in a midair helicopter collision during firefighting operations west of Athens.
England and Wales recorded their driest July in nearly 200 years of recordkeeping, according to the Met Office.
Hungary reduced output at the Paks nuclear power plant to little more than 10% capacity due to low Danube water levels.
The Romanian military detonated a rocky outcrop in the Danube to direct cooling water flow to the Cernavoda nuclear power plant.
Carmakers Dacia and Ford agreed to suspend automotive production in Romania until August 19 due to the national energy crisis.
Water levels on the River Rhine dropped to historic record lows at Cologne in Germany and Lobith in the Netherlands.
Romanian naval forces used 180 kg of explosives in a controlled underwater explosion to restore water flow near Cernavoda.
France evacuated over 224,000 people due to a massive wildfire burning 420 square kilometres in the country's largest civilian evacuation outside wartime.
Aung San Suu Kyi met an International Committee of the Red Cross delegation led by Arnaud de Baecque in Naypyitaw.
Aung San Suu Kyi was detained in 2021 after a military coup and sentenced to 33 years in prison before being moved to house arrest.
Kim Aris described his mother's meeting with the Red Cross representative as the first positive development concerning her in over five years.
Official photos released by Myanmar authorities showed Aung San Suu Kyi cutting an 81st birthday cake.
A Yangon court sentenced former lawmaker Saw Naing to three years in prison for organizing a religious ceremony on Aung San Suu Kyi's birthday.
The Japanese yen strengthened to 155 to the US dollar following a joint currency intervention by Japan and the United States.
Prior to the market intervention, the Japanese yen had fallen to a 40-year low of nearly 164 to the US dollar.
Bank of Japan data indicated Tokyo spent as much as $36.58 billion on Friday to support the yen.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted on his cabinet meeting pad a task to buy $5 billion to $10 billion worth of Japanese yen.
The market intervention was the first joint foreign exchange action conducted by the United States and Japan since March 2011.
The Bank of Japan maintained its main interest rate at 1% while the US Federal Reserve's benchmark rate stood between 3.50% and 3.75%.
Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin fled Russia to Paris as government pressure intensified.
Russia's justice ministry designated Boris Nadezhdin as a foreign agent and barred him from parliamentary elections.
Boris Nadezhdin was charged with displaying extremist symbols over a 10-second image of Alexei Navalny in a reposted social media video.
Russian electoral authorities barred Boris Nadezhdin from running in the 2024 presidential election citing flawed candidate signatures.
Boris Nadezhdin posted a video from Paris confirming he had left Russia after being prevented from running for parliament.
Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor won the Bankipur Assembly byelection in Bihar, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes.
BJP candidate Satish Govindbhai Patel won the Manjalpur Assembly seat in Gujarat by a margin of 30,630 votes.
Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh won the Datia Assembly byelection in Madhya Pradesh by 6,016 votes.
Independent candidates named Lalu Prasad Yadav and Nitish Kumar received 81 and 149 votes respectively in Bankipur, losing their security deposits.
The BJP had held the Bankipur Assembly seat in Bihar for over three decades since 1995 prior to Prashant Kishor's victory.
The Bankipur seat became vacant after BJP leader Nitin Nabin resigned upon his election to the Rajya Sabha and elevation to BJP national president.
A New Delhi court acquitted former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in a sexual harassment case filed by six female wrestlers.
Wrestler Vinesh Phogat stated that the complainants will appeal Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's acquittal in a higher court.
Prominent wrestlers including Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, and Bajrang Punia launched a sit-in protest against Singh at Jantar Mantar in April 2023.
Delhi Police registered two FIRs against Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in April 2023 following complaints by female wrestlers.
A Delhi court accepted a police closure report in a POCSO case against Singh in May 2025 after a minor complainant withdrew her allegations.
Former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar was acquitted of criminal intimidation charges by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwini Panwar.
